Summary of today's discovery:
- Goal: Integrate Redwood inference into Acme's product search & Q&A flow (low-latency reranker + structured tool calling for actions).
- Constraints: PCI-adjacent data; preference for private VPC deployment or dedicated capacity; strict prompt governance and audit requirements.
- Success metrics: end-to-end latency < 300ms P95 for short queries, reranker improves CTR by +10%, and ability to rollback prompt changes quickly.

Immediate next steps (owners):
1) We'll send SDK quickstart + auth options (Marissa)  — attachment and drive link below.
2) Tech dive on routing, embeddings + reranker architecture (Dev Patel / Rishi)  — propose 60m next week.
3) Prompt governance / red-team kickoff to cover versioning, injection mitigations, and eval set (Rishi)  — propose dates below.

Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AcmeRedwoodIntegration

Thanks Marissa  I appreciate the recap. A few clarification items from our engineering and security teams: 

1) Auth: For hosted demo we'll accept API key, but for production we need either mTLS or OIDC with our internal IdP. Do you support OIDC flows or a way to federate tokens?
2) Routing & failover: If we have spike traffic, can we route to a cheaper model variant with graceful degradation (we discussed fallback earlier)? Need to understand how routing policies are configured (per-route, per-tenant).
3) Embeddings + reranker: We liked the two-stage approach you mentioned  — want an explicit example of index pipeline + reranker step and how it affects cost/latency.
4) Prompt governance: We need example prompt templates and a versioning strategy. Also concerned about prompt injection  — what mitigations do you recommend and do you run red-team style tests?

If you can loop in an SE for the tech deep-dive that would be great. We can do Tue/Wed next week mornings PST.

Great questions  — looping in Dev Patel (SE) and Rishi (Applied ML) to handle the technical details.

Quick answers while they prep a deeper doc/tech dive: 
- Auth: Hosted API supports API keys and optional OAuth/OIDC for delegated access. For Dedicated/Private we support OIDC federation or mTLS and can provide KMS integration for keys.
- Routing: Routing policies are configurable per-tenant and per-route; we can set model priority, cost tiers, and automatic fallback to compatible variants.
- Embeddings/reranker: We'll share an example pipeline doc (indexing frequency, ANN config, reranker model choice) — Dev will attach a short reference.
- Prompt governance: We have example prompt templates and a suggested versioning scheme (semantic prompt versions stored in config; audit logs for system prompt changes). Rishi will add details on red-team playbooks and injection mitigations.

Proposed tech-dive slots: Tue 2026-10-27 09:00-10:00 PST or Wed 2026-10-28 10:00-11:00 PST. Which works best?

Marissa
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.example>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Redwood integration + prompt governance  — technical notes

Hi Todd/Sasha  — thanks for the detailed notes. Below are concrete integration recommendations and references before our tech dive. I'll bring a short demo.

1) SDK setup and auth
- Quickstart: use the Redwood SDK (Node/Python). Samples attached: redwood_sdk_quickstart.pdf.
- Auth options:
  * Hosted: API keys (short-lived optional), OAuth/OIDC for delegated flows.
  * Dedicated/Private: OIDC federation to your IdP or mTLS with client certs + KMS for key rotation.
  * Recommendation: Start with OAuth/OIDC for production; API keys for PoC.

2) Routing & model variants
- Config lives in per-tenant routing policies. You can define rules by endpoint, latency SLO, or cost tier.
- Automatic fallback: we support policy-based fallback to compatible quantized variants. Example: policy = {route: /search, primary: reranker-v2, fallback: reranker-v1-quantized}.

3) Structured output & tool-calling
- We support function/tool calling via a JSON schema-based contract (similar to OpenAI function calling). The SDK returns structured JSON and includes input validation hooks to minimize risky tool invocations.

4) Embeddings + reranker pattern
- Recommended pipeline:
  1) Precompute 1536-d embeddings using a production embedding model and store in ANN index (HNSW/FAISS) with monthly reindexing.
  2) On query: retrieve top-K candidates via ANN (K=100), then run a lightweight transformer reranker (cross-attention) on the top 10 for precision.
  3) To reduce cost, use cached candidate sets and result-level caching for frequent queries.
- Latency: expect ANN retrieval ~10-20ms, reranker 40-120ms depending on model size.

5) Prompt templates, versioning, and injection mitigations
- Prompt templates: attach example_prompt_templates.md (includes system prompt, few-shot examples, and structured output templates).
- Versioning: store prompts in a config repo with semantic prompt versions (e.g., prompt_v1.2). Changes require PRs, code review, and are linked to an eval bundle. All changes are timestamped and recorded in the audit log.
- Injection mitigations:
  * Input sanitization: strip or canonicalize user-supplied delimiters when merging into system prompts.
  * Length/role separation: never append raw user text into system-level instructions; use explicit placeholders and strict parser for structured outputs.
  * Tool access control: the model must call tools via a validated function schema; tool invocations are audited and can be gated by runtime predicates.
  * Monitoring: continuous evals and anomaly detection on output distributions (BLEU, hallucination flags, DM metrics).

Attachments: redwood_sdk_quickstart.pdf, example_prompt_templates.md

Happy to expand any of the items in the tech dive  — propose we allocate 20m to auth/routing and 25m to embeddings/reranker + prompts.

—Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: Redwood integration + prompt governance  — red-team + governance plan

Todd/Sasha  — I can run the red-team / prompt governance session. Proposed plan and asks below: 

1) Governance baseline
- Store all system prompts and templates in a git-backed repo (internal or a restricted Drive). Each update requires a PR, description of expected behavioral changes, and linkage to an evaluation bundle.
- Tag prompt versions semantically (prompt_v1.0, prompt_v1.1, etc.). Use feature flags to rollout prompts to a % of traffic with automatic rollback on metric regressions.

2) Prompt injection testing (red-team)
- We'll run automated adversarial test generation against the prompt templates and a manual red-team to try real-world injections. Results feed an issues tracker for fixes.
- Examples of mitigations we use: structured output schema enforcement, role separation, and a validation layer that rejects outputs that violate schema.

3) Monitoring & rollback
- Continuous evals over a curated test set + live production probes. If error/hallucination rates exceed thresholds, we automatically revert to previous prompt version and notify stakeholders.

4) Next steps & scheduling
- Tech dive: Tue 2026-10-27 09:00-10:00 PST (accepted unless you prefer Wed).
- Red-team kickoff: 2026-11-03 10:00-12:00 PST  — 2h workshop + 1-week automated sweep.

Please confirm the tech-dive slot and whether the red-team date works. I'll prepare a short red-team playbook and share prior artifacts.

Thanks,
